arxiv-2411-00721.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
arxiv-2411-00721.creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland
arxiv-2411-00721.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland. A Boolean function f f on k k bits induces a shift-invariant vectorial Boolean function F F from n n bits to n n bits for every n ≥ k n\geq k . If F F is bijective for every n n , we say that f f is a proper lifting, and it is known that proper liftings are exactly those functions that arise as local rules of reversible cellular automata.

pmc-11346567.title: The role of mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 in knee osteoarthritis inflammation
pmc-11346567.creator: Dingchang He, Xin Liu, Wenhao Yang, Taiyuan Guan, Guoyou Wang
pmc-11346567.description: Mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 is known to mediate a variety of inflammatory pathways and is also involved in the occurrence and development of many orthopedic diseases. Although its role in the inflammatory mechanism of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) has been reported, a systematic explanation is yet to be seen.

pmc-12417620.title: Proteomic and non-proteomic changes of presynaptic proteins in animal models of Alzheimer's disease: A meta-analysis 2015–2023
pmc-12417620.creator: Anne Anschuetz, Karima Schwab, Charles R Harrington, Claude M Wischik, Gernot Riedel
pmc-12417620.description: BackgroundSynaptic proteins are often used as markers for synaptic damage in non-clinical models of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and are known to be affected early in the disease in humans. Presynaptic protein loss has been shown to be especially strong in patients, though not all proteins and brain areas are affected equally.

pmc-12550363.title: Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Among Adolescents and Young Adults, NHANES 2009–2014
pmc-12550363.creator: Rushelle L Byfield, Eunhee Choi, Jordana B Cohen, Ian M Kronish, Michael Rakotz, Daichi Shimbo
pmc-12550363.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BACKGROUNDAmong middle-aged and older adults, home blood pressure (BP) monitoring (HBPM) is a tool for both diagnosis and management of hypertension. Pediatric guidelines recommend HBPM as an adjunct to office BP measurement among children and adolescents with hypertension.

pmc-13202135.title: Intensive weight loss intervention versus usual care for adults with severe and complex obesity: the LightWAY randomised trial protocol
pmc-13202135.creator: Sarah Wane, Paul Aveyard, Sabrina Wielsøe, Sofus Christian Larsen, Jadine Scragg, Jane Lindschou, Janus Christian Jakobsen, Janus Engstrøm, Ina Olmer Specht, Ann-Kathrin Lindahl Christiansen, Aksel Karl Georg Jensen, Thomas Bandholm, Charlotte Albury, Gritt Overbeck, Susanne Reventlow, Kim Rose Olse
pmc-13202135.description: IntroductionEffective treatment for clinical obesity is available but is rarely offered by healthcare systems, which often treat complications without treating the underlying cause. The LightWAY trial will investigate the clinical benefits and harms as well as cost-effectiveness of an intensive weight loss intervention compared with existing weight management programmes for people with clinical obesity.

pmc-13358232.title: Concomitant medication reporting should accompany fecal microbiota transplantation plus anti-PD-1 therapy in gastric cancer
pmc-13358232.creator: Guofu Mao, Haizhen Lan
pmc-13358232.description: This commentary discusses the phase I study of fecal microbiota transplantation plus anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy in refractory microsatellite-stable gastric cancer. We suggest that this strategy should be treated as a pharmacomicrobiomic intervention rather than only as an immunotherapy combination.

pmc-13522653.title: Electrophysiological Correlates of Encoding Indicate Altered Processing but Comparable Subsequent Memory Effects Across Virtual Reality and Desktop‐Based Conditions
pmc-13522653.creator: Joanna Kisker, Merle Sagehorn, Thomas Gruber
pmc-13522653.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Successful episodic memory formation emerges from the interplay of perceptual, attentional, contextual, and elaborative processes. The relative contribution of these processes to encoding may vary with the conditions under which information is encountered. In particular, different presentation modalities, like virtual reality (VR) and desktop‐based presentations (PC), can convey the same semantic identity of an item while differing in perceptual, spatial, and contextual information.

pmc-13564765.title: Distinguishing Benign from Malignant Small Enhancing Breast Lesions Using Radiomics
pmc-13564765.creator: Parlyn Hatch, Christopher Louviere, Mutlu Mete, Oswaldo A. Guevara Tirado, Ruben G. Ortiz Cordero, Hector Diaz De Villegas, Kazim Z. Gumus
pmc-13564765.description: Background/Objectives: Small enhancing lesions (often termed foci if lesion ≤ 5 mm) observed on breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pose a persistent challenge. Their clinical relevance and the most effective management strategy remain unclear, often leading to unnecessary biopsies. We sought to uncover whether quantitative radiomic features of these lesions could reliably discriminate malignant ones from benign ones.

uslaw-usc-t1-s6.title: 1 U.S.C. § 6 — Limitation of term “products of American fisheries”
uslaw-usc-t1-s6.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t1-s6.description: United States Code, Title 1 (General Provisions); Chapter 1 (Rules Of Construction). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Wherever, in the statutes of the United States or in the rulings, regulations, or interpretations of various administrative bureaus and agencies of the United States there appears or may appear the term “products of American fisheries” said term shall not include fresh or frozen fish.
